Set the initial stop for mean‑reversion and short/fade trades at least 1.5 × the asset’s 14‑day ATR to avoid premature exits caused by normal volatility.
Move the stop to breakeven or begin trailing once the trade is 0.5 R in profit, rather than waiting for a 0.2 R threshold.
Do not execute long cryptocurrency trades when the broader market regime is classified as risk-off.

recaps.title: October 2026 Season Recap: A Bruising Road Trip
recaps.body:
Erwann, think of October like an ugly mid-season road trip where we took some hard hits on the scoreboard.

**The Standings:**
We finished 8-28. Our account slid from $10,000 to $7,928.44 (-20.7%), while the S&P 500 merely dipped 1.7% to $9,833. We definitely lost ground in the division.

**Trade of the Month (Highlight Reel):**
Our short on Boeing (BA). Arjun's quant momentum squad nailed the breakdown, patiently riding it down into our $173 target for a clean +$217 profit (+2.23R). Textbook execution.

**The Worst Trade (Costly Fumble):**
Intel (INTC) earnings. We went long expecting an upside pop, but horrific forward guidance caused an unholy gap-down past our stop, exiting near $66 for a -$495 loss (-4.18R). Big lesson: never step in front of high-volatility earnings without strict gap protection.

**Comeback Story & Staffing Drama:**
Despite the slump, Ashley Brennan kept the locker room unified—zero pink slips handed out. Meanwhile, our interns (Sienna, Dev, and Zoe) quietly stayed in the green with ~$140 equity each, giving the veterans a run for their money.

**MVP:**
Elena Castillo took the crown, delivering a stellar 67% win rate across a massive 577 research decisions. Special nod to Nadia Volkov, who correctly called the bear tape 60% of the time.

**Next Month’s Gameplan:**
We're benching naked earnings gambles, letting Elena call the offensive plays, and rebuilding the bankroll with disciplined base hits.

letters.title: Weekly Desk Update – 2026-10-18
letters.body:
Dear Erwann,

Our $10,000 paper account finished the week at $9,527.61, a 4.73% decline. By contrast the S&P 500 proxy fell only 0.72% (from 10,000 to 9,928). The gap tells us the desk under‑performed the market, largely because our tactical bucket generated a net loss of $412.50 across ten closed trades (30% win‑rate, avg R ‑0.35).

**Best trades** – The USD/JPY trend‑pullback long produced a modest $10.35 profit (R +0.15) and the RKLX mean‑reversion long gave $40.05 (R +0.27). Both succeeded because the price respected the 20‑day SMA before moving in our favour and we allowed enough room for the move to develop.

**Worst trades** – The DOGE/USD mean‑reversion long lost $91.09 (R ‑1.03) and the EUR/GBP long lost $162.88 (R ‑1.36). In each case we entered on an oversold signal while the asset was below multiple moving averages and fundamental pressure was strongly negative. The trade was stopped out quickly, confirming that the signal alone was insufficient.

**What worked** – Trend‑pullback entries that waited for a bounce off a key SMA and used a trailing stop captured small upside without being clipped by a hard time‑stop. The RKLX trade exemplifies this.

**What didn’t** – Over‑reliance on extreme oversold/overbought readings, especially on assets with weak fundamentals (FMC, EUR/GBP, DOGE). Tight intraday time‑stops also ate into winners (USD/JPY, USD/CHF) and forced premature exits on losers.

**Caution vs. looseness** – The engine skipped 49 ideas, many of which were short signals on crypto (DOGE, HYPE) that our long‑only crypto rule blocked. Those missed shorts would have been profitable, suggesting we are too restrictive on the short side. At the same time, our time‑stop discipline is too loose, cutting winners before they can realise their expected R.

**Plan for next week** – 1) Add a confirmation filter for mean‑reversion trades (price must test a support level and show a bounce). 2) Replace hard intraday time‑stops with dynamic trailing stops for any trade with expected R > 0.2. 3) Open a short‑crypto lane for high‑probability short ideas that meet our risk criteria. We will keep position sizing modest (max 2% of equity per trade) and monitor draw‑down closely.

Regards,
The AI Trading Desk

letters.title: Desk Letter: Week Ending October 25, 2026
letters.body:
Erwann,

This week was an unvarnished setback for the desk. Our paper account declined 8.89%, falling from $9,543.21 to $8,694.61. Over the same stretch, our S&P 500 benchmark dipped just 0.42% (from 9,928.07 to 9,886.32). Our heavy underperformance stemmed from aggressive counter-trend positioning and poor risk management on the short side.

Our best closed trade was a short on GBP/JPY, netting +$46.38 (+0.47 R). The thesis played out as forecast, but an arbitrary 1–5 day time stop closed the position prematurely, leaving significant profit on the table. Our worst trade was a short on SMCI, which cost us -$204.43 (-1.83 R). We attempted to fade momentum into earnings/catalyst optimism, and the stock triggered a violent short squeeze that overshot our intended stop-loss.

What worked: directional macro forecasts when aligned with technical structure. What failed completely: fighting strong trends across FX (USD/MXN short, EUR/CHF long) and catching falling knives in crypto (ADA and UNI longs both took full -1.0 R stops).

Regarding discipline, the desk was simultaneously too loose on trade entries and too timid on trade management. We took 14 closed setups across noisy instruments with an unacceptable 14% win rate this week. Yet on our two winning trades (GBP/JPY and IONQ), we clamped profits early with rigid calendar time stops rather than letting the thesis run. On the passing side, the engine properly filtered out multiple weak altcoins (DOT, ONDO, AAVE), which prevented further bleed.

Our historical backtests clearly confirm that shorting overbought conditions has negative expectancy across thousands of trials (-0.104 R average). For next week, we are eliminating unhedged equity shorts in high-beta momentum names, requiring verified reversal candle confirmation on all mean-reversion entries, and enforcing wider profit targets for winning positions.

Dear Erwann,

Our paper account slipped from $8,615.81 to $7,923.24 this week – a $692.57 loss (‑8.0%). The S&P 500 fell only $53.32 (‑0.5%), so we under‑performed the market by a wide margin. The gap is almost entirely the result of a handful of losing ideas that blew up our risk budget.

**Best trades** – The short on Boeing (BA) delivered $219.34 (+2.23 R) and the long on Iren (IREN) added $100.85 (+1.13 R). Both were mean‑reversion plays that respected our higher‑low confirmation rule and used trailing stops, allowing the price to run while protecting gains. The MSFT momentum long also worked (+$81.09, +0.95 R) but was cut early by a hard time‑stop, leaving money on the table.

**Worst trades** – Intel (INTC) was the single biggest loser, a $494.33 loss (‑4.18 R) after an earnings surprise turned the trade into a gap‑down. LMT short (‑$103.32, ‑0.93 R) and Robinhood long (‑$121.76, ‑1.10 R) also hurt, each being stopped out on a time‑based exit despite still having upside potential. Our crypto pull‑back longs (BCH/USD, etc.) all hit full‑risk stops, confirming that the current crypto rule set is too permissive.

**What worked / didn’t** – Trailing stops on mean‑reversion trades proved valuable; hard time‑stops repeatedly killed winners (MSFT) and forced losers out before the signal could reverse (USD_CHF, EUR_GBP). Earnings‑play ideas performed abysmally (0 % win rate) and should be trimmed. The engine skipped 22 ideas, many of which were short‑crypto or short‑fade forex setups that would have been negative anyway, so we were not overly cautious – we were simply unlucky on the few ideas we took.

**Next‑week plan** – 1) Cut earnings‑play exposure to zero until we rebuild a positive edge. 2) Switch all time‑stops on tactical trades to trailing stops once the trade moves 0.2 R in our favor. 3) Add a macro filter for short/fade forex: only trade when the USD is weakening (risk‑off). 4) Tighten crypto participation to “no‑trade” until we develop a dedicated high‑probability rule set.

We’ll keep the focus on quant‑momentum and disciplined mean‑reversion, where the data still shows a positive edge.

Regards,
Your AI Trading Desk

letters.title: Weekly Desk Update – 9 Nov 2026
letters.body:
Dear Erwann,

Our $10,000 paper account posted a modest +1.71% gain this week, moving from $7,820.71 to $7,954.14, while the S&P 500 equivalent fell about –2.6% (9833 → 9573.8). In absolute terms we added $133, a small but meaningful out‑performance given the broader market weakness.

**Best trade – NZD/USD (short, macro)**
We entered at 0.56815 on a down‑trend thesis, moved the stop to breakeven and trailed it to 0.5565. The pair slid to 0.5558, delivering a +$278 P&L and a 1.45 R return. The disciplined trailing‑stop/scale‑out approach protected the profit and prevented the position from eroding.

**Worst trades**
*USD/CAD (long, trend‑pullback)* – The pair failed to bounce off the 50‑day SMA and hit our 1‑5‑day time‑stop, costing –$62 (‑0.68 R). The loss highlights the danger of relying on a time‑stop when macro news can suppress the expected rebound.
*EUR/JPY (short, short/fade)* – A short‑term bounce triggered a tight 176.70 stop, resulting in a –$85 loss (‑1.01 R). Our stop was too close to normal ATR volatility.
*LINK/USD (long, quant momentum)* – A sudden 7× volume spike proved a transient sell‑off; the stop was barely away from entry, forcing an emergency exit at –$59 (‑0.86 R).

**What worked** – The macro‑driven NZD/USD trade and the use of a trailing stop once the trade was in profit. Both underscore the value of dynamic risk management.

**What didn’t** – Over‑tight stops on EUR/JPY and LINK, and the reliance on a hard time‑stop for USD/CAD. Both resulted in premature exits and negative R‑values.

**Caution vs. looseness** – The engine skipped 30 ideas, many of which were crypto longs that our historical record flags as negative EV. In this case the filter was appropriate; we were not overly cautious.

**Plan for next week** – 1) Apply an ATR‑based stop buffer (≥1.5 × ATR) on all mean‑reversion and short/fade entries. 2) Move stops to breakeven or trail once a trade reaches 0.5 R profit. 3) Reserve time‑stops for trades with a clearly low expected R (≤0.2 R) and avoid them on pull‑back setups. We’ll continue to monitor macro filters and tighten our risk‑management discipline.

Regards,
The AI Trading Desk

letters.title: Weekly Desk Update: Macro FX Precision and Capital Preservation
letters.body:
Erwann,

For the week, the desk posted a solid gain, with our account value advancing from $7,932.25 to $8,108.79 (+2.23%), modestly outpacing the S&P 500 benchmark equivalent's gain from 9,573.77 to 9,782.14 (+2.18%). Cumulative realized PnL sits at -$1,816.32, but this week demonstrated the value of patience and tighter strategy selection.

We closed two trades this week, both in our tactical macro bucket, and both hit their predefined profit targets. USD/CAD was our best performer, locking in +1.66R (+$110.17) after sustaining its bullish channel into our 1.4240 target. USD/CHF also executed cleanly, delivering +0.62R (+$43.68) on a thesis supported by favorable interest rate differentials and carry. Macro continues to be our standout style, now 3-for-3 with an average return of +1.24R and $432.08 in cumulative gains.

The most critical story of the week, however, was our selectivity. The execution engine reviewed 25 setups and skipped 21. Reviewing the post-decision data, this restraint was precisely calibrated rather than overly cautious. Skipping long crypto attempts saved us from severe drawdowns—notably UNI/USD, which plummeted -10.22% after being rejected. Bypassing speculative longs like ARM (-1.34%) similarly preserved capital. Our historical 0% win rate in crypto and persistent friction in equity mean-reversion made these passes mandatory under our current risk parameters.

Our edge tilt remains at 0.7x, appropriately sizing down overall risk until cumulative metrics recover from earlier drawdown periods. For next week, we will continue prioritizing macro currency pairs and quantitative momentum where our data confirms positive expectancy, while maintaining a strict zero-tolerance policy on counter-trend crypto bids during risk-off regimes.
